migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration programme governance: appoint programme lead, define RACI, secure executive sponsorship, and document scope covering the four cryptographic assets and the 10-15 year data confidentiality requirement.
prerequisites: Executive management approval of programme mandate
Budget allocation of USD 250,000 confirmed by finance

migration_steps.activity: Perform comprehensive cryptographic inventory and data classification: catalogue all RSA-2048 TLS certificates, ECDSA P-256 API authentication keys, RSA-3072 key-wrapping keys, and ECDH P-256 channels; map data flows and identify which protected data has confidentiality lifetime of 10-15 years.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Access to configuration management databases, certificate inventories, and application owners

migration_steps.activity: Conduct harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) risk assessment: quantify exposure for long-lived sensitive customer data protected by RSA-3072 key wrapping and ECDH P-256 channels; assign risk ratings and prioritise assets by data confidentiality lifetime and exposure surface.
prerequisites: Cryptographic inventory completed (step 2)
Data classification and retention schedule available

migration_steps.activity: Engage Thales in writing to obtain confirmed PQC support status for Luna Network HSM 7: request firmware roadmap, ML-KEM and ML-DSA algorithm support, FIPS validation status, API/SDK compatibility, and delivery timeline. Do not assume support until written confirmation is received.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Defined technical requirements for HSM PQC capabilities

migration_steps.activity: Engage third-party core banking platform vendor in writing to obtain PQC compatibility confirmation, migration roadmap, supported algorithms (ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA for signatures), and any contractual or certification constraints.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Defined interface and dependency map for core banking platform

migration_steps.activity: Develop target PQC architecture and migration design: define hybrid modes (classical + ML-KEM for key establishment, classical + ML-DSA for signatures) where appropriate, specify crypto-agility requirements, and produce design documents for each asset class.
prerequisites: HNDL risk assessment completed (step 3)
Initial vendor responses received (steps 4 and 5) or documented as pending

migration_steps.activity: Procure non-production laboratory environment for PQC testing: isolated lab HSM (if vendor confirms PQC-capable firmware or evaluation units), software PQC libraries (e.g., OpenSSL 3.x with ML-KEM/ML-DSA), and test certificates. Procurement must not assume production HSM PQC capability.
prerequisites: Budget approval for lab equipment within USD 250,000 envelope
Vendor engagement responses clarifying evaluation unit availability (step 4)

migration_steps.activity: Conduct non-production lab testing of ML-KEM for key establishment and ML-DSA for digital signatures: validate interoperability, performance, and integration with existing applications; test hybrid modes; document results and gaps.
prerequisites: Lab environment procured and configured (step 7)
Target architecture design completed (step 6)
Written confirmation of HSM lab/evaluation capabilities from Thales (step 4)

migration_steps.activity: Prepare production migration runbooks, rollback plans, and operational approval packages for prioritised assets (RSA-3072 key wrapping and ECDH P-256 channels first, given HNDL exposure). Submit for change advisory board review.
prerequisites: Lab testing results documented (step 8)
Vendor written confirmations for production support (steps 4 and 5)
Regulatory and compliance review completed

migration_steps.activity: Execute production cryptographic changes for highest-priority assets (RSA-3072 key wrapping to hybrid ML-KEM, ECDH P-256 channels to hybrid ML-KEM) only after all vendor confirmations, lab validation, and operational approvals are in place. Schedule outside the change freeze (1 Dec 2026 - 15 Jan 2027 inclusive).
prerequisites: Written confirmation from Thales of production HSM PQC support and firmware compatibility (step 4)
Written confirmation from core banking vendor of PQC compatibility where applicable (step 5)
Successful lab testing and interoperability validation (step 8)
Change advisory board approval and completed runbooks (step 9)
Change freeze lifted (after 2027-01-15)

migration_steps.activity: Plan and execute HSM firmware upgrade to PQC-capable version, if and only if Thales provides written confirmation of production support, compatibility, and validated firmware. Schedule outside the change freeze.
prerequisites: Written confirmation from Thales of production PQC firmware availability, compatibility, and FIPS validation (step 4)
Lab validation of firmware in non-production environment (step 8)
Operational approval and change advisory board sign-off
Change freeze lifted (after 2027-01-15)

migration_steps.activity: Migrate RSA-2048 TLS certificates to hybrid or ML-KEM-based key establishment and ML-DSA-based signatures where applicable, following successful validation and vendor confirmations. This is a major application deployment and must wait for all dependencies.
prerequisites: HSM production PQC support confirmed in writing (step 4)
Core banking vendor PQC compatibility confirmed in writing (step 5)
Lab testing and interoperability validation completed (step 8)
Production runbooks and rollback plans approved (step 9)
Change freeze lifted (after 2027-01-15)

migration_steps.activity: Migrate ECDSA P-256 internal API authentication signatures to ML-DSA, following successful validation and vendor confirmations. This is a major application deployment and must wait for all dependencies.
prerequisites: HSM production PQC support confirmed in writing (step 4)
Core banking vendor PQC compatibility confirmed in writing (step 5)
Lab testing and interoperability validation completed (step 8)
Production runbooks and rollback plans approved (step 9)
Change freeze lifted (after 2027-01-15)

blockers.blocker: Thales has not confirmed production support, firmware compatibility, or delivery timeline for NIST-standardized ML-KEM and ML-DSA on the Luna Network HSM 7.
blockers.reason: Without written confirmation, no production cryptographic changes requiring HSM-backed PQC operations can be safely executed. Assuming support would violate the constraint against inventing vendor capabilities and could cause service disruption or security gaps.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written confirmation from Thales including: supported PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA), firmware version and compatibility matrix, FIPS 140-3 validation status, API/SDK support, and production delivery timeline. Validate in non-production lab before any production change.

blockers.blocker: Third-party core banking platform vendor has not provided written confirmation of PQC compatibility or a migration roadmap.
blockers.reason: The core banking platform may be unable to support ML-KEM or ML-DSA, or may require vendor-specific upgrades. Production migration of dependent assets cannot proceed without confirmed compatibility and a supported migration path.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written confirmation from the core banking vendor including: PQC compatibility status, supported algorithms, required version upgrades, migration roadmap, and any contractual or certification constraints. Validate integration in non-production lab.

blockers.blocker: Procurement of PQC-capable lab HSM or evaluation units is dependent on Thales confirming availability and terms.
blockers.reason: Lab testing of ML-KEM and ML-DSA with HSM-backed operations cannot be fully validated without appropriate hardware. Software-only testing may not reflect production HSM behaviour.
blockers.resolution_required: Confirm with Thales the availability of evaluation units or lab-licensed PQC-capable firmware. If unavailable, document limitations and rely on software PQC libraries for initial lab testing, clearly noting the gap.

blockers.blocker: Interoperability and performance of ML-KEM and ML-DSA with existing applications, TLS stacks, and API authentication mechanisms is unvalidated.
blockers.reason: Without lab validation, production deployment risks service disruption, performance degradation, or security weaknesses. Hybrid modes and crypto-agility must be proven before production.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete non-production lab testing (step 8) covering interoperability, performance, and hybrid mode behaviour. Document results and remediate gaps before production approval.

blockers.blocker: Mandatory infrastructure change freeze from 1 December 2026 through 15 January 2027 inclusive prohibits production cryptographic changes, HSM firmware upgrades, and major application deployments.
blockers.reason: Any production migration activity scheduled during this period would violate the freeze and risk operational stability. Only planning, documentation, vendor engagement, and permitted non-production lab activities may continue.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes, HSM firmware upgrades, and major deployments after 2027-01-15. Use the freeze period for planning, documentation, and vendor follow-up where permitted.

blockers.blocker: Regulatory approval and compliance review for PQC algorithm use in production has not been completed.
blockers.reason: Banking regulators may require notification or approval before deploying new cryptographic algorithms in production systems handling customer data. Premature deployment could breach regulatory obligations.
blockers.resolution_required: Engage compliance and regulatory affairs to determine notification or approval requirements for ML-KEM and ML-DSA. Obtain necessary approvals before production changes.

vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written confirmation of production support for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, firmware version and compatibility matrix, FIPS 140-3 validation status, API/SDK support, and delivery timeline. Lab validation results demonstrating interoperability.

Written confirmation of PQC compatibility, supported algorithms (ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA for signatures), required version upgrades, migration roadmap, and any contractual or certification constraints. Lab integration validation results.
